svg.text: Hexapod — Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W wiring schematic
Xbox controller (Bluetooth) → Pi Zero 2 W → UART on the Servo 2040 SDA/SCL pins → 18 servos · RPLIDAR C1 on USB (planned)
Pi’s inner USB port, not PWR IN
USB power for the Servo 2040 processor (power-only lead is fine)
≥ 3 A: Pi, hub, LiDAR, board logic
Thonny / Motion Studio: plug into the
Servo 2040 USB-C instead of the hub lead
1. VERIFY on the Servo 2040 pinout that SDA = GP20 and SCL = GP21 (UART1 TX/RX).
2. Cross the wires: Pi TX → Servo RX, Pi RX ← Servo TX. Join GND. Do NOT join 3V3.
3. Both boards use 3.3 V logic: no level shifter. Keep UART wires under 20–30 cm.
4. Power the Pi from its own 5 V regulator (5 V and GND), never from the servo rail directly.
5. Common ground: battery −, buck converter, Pi and Servo 2040 GND are all joined.
6. Switch the servo power off before connecting or disconnecting anything.
7. RPLIDAR C1: connect through its USB adapter and the hub. The Pi’s GPIO UART is used by the Servo 2040 and its other UART by Bluetooth.
LiDAR: check pinout on its datasheet
